item.title: In 1888, George Vanderbilt began building a vast North Carolina estate; 26 years later, his widow...
item.description: In 1914, Edith Vanderbilt made a landmark decision by selling 86,700 acres of land to the federal government for conservation purposes, significantly below market value. This generous act was aimed at promoting her late husband's vision of preserving essential forests. The area ultimately became Pisgah National Forest in 1916, laying the groundwork for ecological protection and setting a visionary example for public land conservation in the eastern U.S.

item.title: In 2022, Naomi Osaka paid $6.3 million for a Los Angeles home then sold it back for...
item.description: Nick and Vanessa Lachey have put their stunning Tarzana estate back on the market, asking for nearly $8.2 million. This luxurious property, which they repurchased from tennis star Naomi Osaka, features a wealth of fitness-oriented amenities added during Osaka's ownership, including a high-end recovery suite and a custom gym. The real estate exchange highlights the ever-evolving landscape of celebrity properties in Los Angeles.

item.title: John Oates’ Colorado ranch built from scratch sells for $6.9M
item.description: John Oates and Aimee Oates turned a barren 4.3-acre land into the picturesque Little Woody Creek Ranch in Colorado. After spending countless holidays there, they decided to sell the property as their visits became less frequent. Initially priced at $6 million, then raised to $7.5 million, the property features a charming five-bedroom log home. By July 2024, they finalized the sale at $6.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Xi Jinping tests Donald Trump with 'Thucydides Trap'
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping asserted that the US and China should work together to avoid conflict. He emphasized that China's rise does not have to threaten the United States' position. Despite past confrontational rhetoric, President Trump responded positively, highlighting their relationship. Critics remain skeptical, arguing that China's military expansion poses significant risks. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stressed the importance of engaging with China amidst these challenges.

item.title: An Alabama man fought a power company over a 74-mile transmission line across his property
item.description: A landowner in Shelby County, Alabama, has secured a temporary court order stopping utility crews from clearing his land. The order halts construction for a new power line project, which would have impacted his property. It was determined that Alabama Power may not have followed proper procedures before initiating condemnation. The landowner argues that the chosen route would divide his property and harm local wildlife.

item.title: Gavin Newsom's San Francisco childhood home listed for $4.5 million after major renovation
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom’s San Francisco childhood home has been listed for $4.5 million after an extensive renovation. The Cole Valley property, where Newsom lived during his early childhood, was originally owned by his maternal grandfather and later inherited by his mother, Tessa. The Newsom family sold the property in the 1970s.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: In New York, 29 million discarded glass bottles were ground into concrete for JPMorgan headquarters
item.description: A groundbreaking skyscraper in Midtown Manhattan ingeniously incorporates 29 million recycled bottles as structural elements, tackling both environmental and construction hurdles. The project innovatively replaces Portland cement with ground-glass pozzolan, dramatically cutting down carbon emissions. Despite the ecological materials, engineers adhered to an expedited construction timeline, while the glass-infused concrete combats urban heat. This pioneering effort has sparked a broader adoption of ground-glass pozzolan in local infrastructure endeavors.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Straitcraft: How geography gives Iran leverage and could do the same for India
item.description: Since the onset of the US-Iran war over 200 days ago, Iran has been strategically utilizing maritime chokepoints such as Hormuz. This has resulted in a marked decline in oil flows, affecting the global economy and forcing the US to reconsider its stance. Concurrently, India is exploring ways to capitalize on its geographical advantages against China.

item.title: Did AI-‘kill chain’ lead to deadly Iran school strike? What report claims
item.description: A devastating missile strike by the US on a school in Minab, Iran, has led to the tragic loss of over 150 lives, including 123 innocent children. Investigations uncovered serious issues in the military’s targeting tactics, pointing to outdated intelligence and a lack of comprehensive civilian harm evaluations. The AI-powered Maven Smart System was crucial in target assessments.

item.title: Minnesota girl, 12, wins $10Kprize for her global anti-hate campaign
item.description: Natalie Flaherty, a 12-year-old from Minnesota, received the Gloria Barron Prize for her initiative against hate. She started her campaign, 'I Stand with Anne', by distributing bracelets that promote kindness. Flaherty's project evolved into a nationwide movement, reaching all 50 states and beyond. She plans to use her prize money to continue her advocacy and educational work on hate.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2000, California packed 662,700 shredded waste tires beneath an I-880 on-ramp; they cut...
item.description: Engineers faced challenges while upgrading a highway interchange in Milpitas due to unstable bay mud. They opted to use shredded waste tires as lightweight fill to prevent ground settlement. This choice reduced weight on the soft soil by 40 percent and saved significant project costs. Over two decades, the infrastructure has shown no maintenance issues or structural damage.
